emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Grand Touring 6-speed with the preferred brown leather interior and an apparent PRHT. Black paint is acceptable rather than preferred, and it is NC rather than ND. Smoked tail lamps are a small cheap modification.

ppi_focus: Paint-meter all panels and inspect bumper covers and supports for the 2016 damage repairs
Underbody corrosion check: rear rockers, subframe mounts, brake and fuel lines (Maryland salt car)
Cycle the PRHT several times; check latches, weatherstrips, drains and dryness under the footwell carpet and pad
Cooling system: expansion tank yellowing or seam crust, radiator end tanks, pressure test
6MT shift quality with fast 2-3 shifts hot; clutch engagement point and slave-cylinder wetness
Rear differential pinion and axle seals; confirm the LSD with no chatter on tight turns
OBD scan for codes and readiness monitors; confirm the stock ECU and intake for California smog
Tire date codes, rear wheel-bearing noise, front lower ball joints and end links
what_would_change_verdict: A Carfax showing the 2016 events were truly cosmetic, with repair invoices, plus a clean underbody, would lift documentation and condition.
A PPI finding structural or frame repair, rot, or a leaking PRHT would move it sharply down.
Cooling-system and fluid records, plus tires under six years old, would lift condition and documentation.
Dealer confirmation of the $15,998 fee-inclusive price would improve price value; refusal of an inspection would be disqualifying.
evidence.mission_note: A manual hardtop GT with the preferred brown interior, well inside budget, so it plausibly fills the enthusiast-bridge role. It is an NC rather than the targeted ND RF, and the reported damage history weakens both comfort and resale.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: a VIN that decodes to a 2014 MX-5 Grand Touring 2.0L, a 6-speed manual, a brown leather interior and apparently the PRHT, all visible in the photos. The dealer's own text discloses two Carfax minor-damage events from 2016 with no repair documentation, contradicting the Autotrader 'No Accident or Damage Reported' badge. Photos also show scuffed lower bumpers front and rear and a worn steering-wheel rim. Pricing is internally inconsistent: $15,998 is described as fee-inclusive, but $16,756 is listed after a rise from $14,520 three days earlier. All of these figures sit below the $18,748 fair-value midpoint. None of the model-critical evidence is provided: cooling-system service, fluid records, roof-cycle and dry-floor proof, an OBD readiness scan, or underbody photos, which matter more on a Maryland-only car. One owner and about 54k miles are dealer claims based on a Carfax that is not attached.
evidence.next_action: Ask RockyCarZ for the full Carfax PDF, lift photos of the underbody, written confirmation of the out-the-door price, and permission for a mobile PPI on their lot before any deposit.
